claims.text: Edge dislocations primarily control the unusual mechanical and thermoelastic behavior of refractory HEAs.
Severe lattice distortions stabilize edge-dislocation cores in refractory HEAs.
Stabilization of edge-dislocation cores raises the activation-energy barrier for dislocation motion.
Edge-dislocation control retards thermal softening and preserves elevated-temperature strength.
NbTaTiV is an example of a single-phase BCC refractory HEA and random multicomponent solid solution.
The proposed initial NbTaTiV-based alloy exhibits marked lattice distortion.
Slight adjustment of refractory-element ratios can controllably vary the degree of lattice distortion.
Controlled aging can alter the relative populations of edge and screw dislocations.
Severe lattice distortion favors edge-dislocation stabilization over the screw-dislocation behavior typical of BCC systems.
Plastic flow in BCC elemental metals and dilute alloys is generally controlled by screw dislocations.
A single-BCC NbTaTiV refractory HEA exhibits temperature-dependent elastic anisotropic deformation.
Single-phase refractory HEAs can retain high yield strength and resist softening at elevated temperatures.
Edge-core stabilization causes both persistent elastic anisotropy and elevated-temperature yield-strength retention.
The interplay between lattice distortion and dislocation mobility governs both mechanical response and thermoelastic behavior.
Enhancing lattice distortion will increase edge-dislocation density.
Enhancing lattice distortion will reduce thermoelastic softening and sustain higher elevated-temperature yield strength relative to a lower-distortion composition.
Samples with larger edge-dislocation populations will show a smaller thermally induced decrease in mechanical properties.
The baseline BCC refractory HEA has mixed dislocation character and the usual thermal softening of conventional alloys.
